title: Redwood technical deep dive - Dedicated vs Hosted (KV cache, batching, quantization)
summary: AE + SE ran a 55-minute technical deep dive focused on Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for OptiRetail's high-throughput recommendation and chat use cases. Covered runtime performance (p95/p99 latencies), KV cache hit strategies, batching windows, quantization options (int8/q4/q8-like), noisy neighbor isolation, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed to run an initial benchmark on a representative seq-len distribution, share scripts, and scope a 2-week pilot on Dedicated with autoscale + reserved capacity. Security docs & pricing to be shared.
action_items: Ethan Liu - share benchmark script + runbook - due 2026-12-15
Priya Rao - provide sample traffic profile and 95th/99th latency SLO targets - due 2026-12-13
Samira Patel - send Dedicated pricing + reserved capacity options and security pack link - due 2026-12-10
next_steps: Redwood to run internal baseline with customer's sample traffic (Ethan)
Customer to share seq-len histogram + sample payload (Priya)
Schedule 30-min follow-up to review benchmark results week of 2026-12-20
transcript:
[00:00] Samira (AE): okay thanks everyone for jumping on, we'll do a technical deep dive on dedicated vs hosted, Ethan's going to drive the runtime details. quick intros please.
[00:12] Carlos (CTO): hey all, Carlos here, we run recommendation + chat on peak times, goal is sub-100ms p95 for short prompts and higher throughput for batch offline reranks.
[00:25] Priya (Infra): Priya, infra lead, worried about noisy neighbor and cost spikes, we have compliance needs too (SOC2, KMS).
[00:34] Ethan (SE): great, let's start with a quick sketch of the serving runtime. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching, kv cache, and kernel selection; in Hosted we multiplex many tenants, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput.
[00:50] Priya: when you say continuous batching, what's the batching window? how do you balance latency?
[00:58] Ethan: default sliding window is 5-10ms for low-latency routes, it grows to hit larger batch targets, we tune by route. for your use-case if you want sub-100ms p95 we usually keep aggressive timeouts and smaller max-batch sizes.
[01:14] Liam (ML Eng): what's throughput per GPU for the models we're looking at (7B family, quantized q4-ish)? numbers please.
[01:22] Ethan: rough ballpark: an A100/80GB with int8/q4 implementation does ~120-200 tokens/sec for autoregressive with mixed batch sizes, depends on seq-len; for long seqs throughput drops. with batching for rerank (short seqs) you can get to several thousand tokens/sec aggregated.
[01:38] Carlos: that variation worries me — noisy neighbor could steal cycles. how strict is isolation on Dedicated?
[01:45] Ethan: Dedicated = reserved capacity. you get a GPU pool pinned to your account, plus autoscale policies you set. Noisy neighbor risk is minimal compared to Hosted, because you don't share the same instances. Hosted has tenancy isolation at process/container level but still multiplexes on nodes.
[01:58] Priya: and SLA? can you guarantee throughput?
[02:02] Samira: Dedicated comes with throughput targets tied to reserved vGPUs / instance count. We can commit to an SLO for sustained throughput with burst policies; for hard guarantees we propose reserved capacity with a small buffer.
[02:16] Priya: ok. about KV cache — our chat system uses long context with a lot of overlap between requests, is prefix caching supported? what's hit-rate realistic?
[02:26] Ethan: yes, we have prefix + KV cache. Hit-rate depends on overlap and session reuse. In our benchmarks for similar customer patterns we saw 60-85% effective token savings on high session locality. Cache eviction uses LRU with pinned entries option for Dedicated.
[02:43] Liam: there are some errors in previous notes where 'KV' got transcribed as 'K V' but ok. how are cached keys persisted in private deploys? encrypted at rest?
[02:51] Ethan: in Private/VPC we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. KV cache metadata can be kept in customer-managed storage; actual token caches are ephemeral in-memory but snapshots for warm-up can be optionally persisted encrypted.
[03:06] Carlos: quantization — does Redwood do post-training quant or do you recommend QAT? any accuracy regressions?
[03:12] Ethan: we support multiple quant paths: q4/q8/int8-like kernels. Post-training quantization is usually fine for retrieval-augmented and chat with small prompts; for sensitive generation (high-quality long outputs) QAT can help. We provide a regression eval harness so you can measure exact delta on your prompts.
[03:30] Priya: can quantization interact badly with KV cache / kernel selection?
[03:35] Ethan: mostly no; quantization affects numeric representation but the runtime picks kernels compatible with the quant format. KV cache operates at token-level embeddings/keys and is agnostic to numeric quant if keys are stored in compatible format — there's an internal conversion step but it's well supported.
[03:50] Samira: real-world tradeoff: quantization reduces memory and increases throughput, but can slightly increase CPU conversion cost on the host; we'll show numbers in the benchmark.
[03:59] [00:04:00] Carlos: latency tails — what's p99 on hosted vs dedicated?
[04:05] Ethan: Hosted p99 can vary due to queueing when traffic bursts; typical p99 for small prompts might be 150-300ms; Dedicated with reserved pools and aggressive batching timeouts you can get p99 under 120ms in our controlled benchmarks. YMMV with seq length spikes.
[04:20] Priya: what about pre-warming and cold-start? on a scale-up event will latency spike?
[04:26] Ethan: we have pre-warm strategies: keep warm workers, KV cache warm-up (persisted snapshots), and gradual ramp autoscaling. Dedicated reduces cold-start risk because capacity is reserved; Hosted can use soft-prewarm but you might see short spikes on big scale-ups.
[04:40] Liam: do you expose metrics we can hook into? token-level latency, queue depth, cache hit rate?
[04:45] Ethan: yes, Console exposes per-route metrics: token latency breakdown, queueing time, batch sizes, KV cache hit/miss rates, and kernel selection traces. We'll share a sample dashboard link.
[04:56] Priya: security — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs —anything else for on-prem?
[05:02] Samira: Private includes SAML SSO, RBAC, full audit logs, and KMS integrations. We also provide SOC2 docs and can arrange an NDA/pen test checklist.
[05:12] [00:05:20] Carlos: cost question — Dedicated reserved vs hosted burst costs, what's typical break-even?
[05:18] Samira: depends on steady-state throughput. If you have predictable load > X tokens/month (we gave a threshold in the deck), Dedicated reserved is often 20-40% cheaper per-token after amortizing reservations and autoscale. Hosted is better for spiky unpredictable loads due to no up-front commit. We'll run a projection once you share traffic profile.
[05:36] Ethan: also remember caching and batching reduce billable tokens, so effective cost can be lower than raw tokens.
[05:42] Priya: about the benchmark — what do you need from us to run realistic tests?
[05:46] Ethan: a seq-length histogram, sample prompt set, average token per request, and target concurrency profile. We'll provide a runner that mimics your client distribution and collects p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cache hit rate, and GPU utilization.
[06:02] Liam: will the runner measure per-request wall-clock from client side? we need end-to-end numbers including network overhead.
[06:07] Ethan: yes, the runner can run from your VPC (we'll provide container) or from our test harness; we recommend running from your network to measure realistic e2e latency.
[06:20] Samira: action items recap in a sec. any other deep technical concerns?
[06:25] Carlos: noisy neighbor — do you have examples where Hosted p99 jumped because of other tenants?
[06:30] Ethan: yes, we had an instance where a large batch job caused queuing; we mitigated with per-tenant queue limits and priority routing but Dedicated removed the problem for that customer. Hosted improvements are ongoing but isolation isn't as strict as reserved Dedicated pools.
[06:45] Priya: about private/on-prem deployment — is the runtime identical? any features missing?
[06:50] Ethan: mostly identical; some managed features like multi-tenant hosted analytics are reduced in Private. Core runtime, KV cache, and batcher are the same C++/CUDA stack. Integration points (KMS, storage) are wired to customer systems.
[07:05] [00:07:10] Samira: quick demo reference — we dropped a deck and a benchmark spreadsheet in the shared drive (link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/optiretail-bench). please review.
[07:18] Priya: thanks, received.
[07:20] Ethan: next, let's propose a concrete benchmark plan: 1) Customer sends traffic profile and sample prompts. 2) Redwood runs hosted baseline + dedicated baseline with quantized and non-quantized configs. 3) Run with KV cache enabled and disabled to show delta. 4) Deliver a results sheet with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util.
[07:41] Carlos: timeline? we need this before end of year to make a Q1 decision.
[07:45] Samira: we can ship the runner and start tests within 48-72 hours of receiving profile; results within 7 days after test start.
[07:52] Liam: light note — please include eval on hallucination/regression tests when quantizing.
[07:56] Ethan: yes, we'll run our eval harness against your prompt list and show delta.
[08:02] [00:08:10] Priya: final questions on routing policies — can you fall back to cheaper model variant when capacity constrained?
[08:08] Ethan: yes, smart routing supports fallback to cheaper/quantized variants; you can define rules per route (latency thresholds, cost budget). It's part of the standard orchestration.
[08:20] Carlos: great. recap and next steps?
[08:24] Samira: recap: Redwood to share benchmark script + runbook (Ethan), customer to send traffic profile & SLOs (Priya), Samira to share pricing + security links. follow-up call week of 12/20.
[08:37] Priya: noted.
[08:40] Carlos: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[08:43] Samira: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[55:00] [END]
